title: John Stones misses speeding letter while at World Cup with England

evidence_packet.title: John Stones misses speeding letter while at World Cup with England
evidence_packet.lead: The England defender drove his £150,000 Range Rover at 43mph near his Cheshire home, a court hears
evidence_packet.summary: The England defender drove his £150,000 Range Rover at 43mph near his Cheshire home, a court hears
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Footballer John Stones has been convicted of speeding after he missed a police letter while at the World Cup with England The 32-year-old defender, who left Manchester City for Inter Milan in the summer, was caught driving his £150,000 Range Rover at 43mph (69 km/h) along a 30 mph (48 km/h) stretch of a country lane near his Cheshire home in May Stones admitted being the driver when first contacted by Cheshire Police, but did not respond to a second letter offering him the chance to pay a fixed penalty to keep the speeding offence out of court He wrote to Warrington Magistrates Court to explain he had been abroad but was landed with a £1,052 court bill. He was given four points Stones was prosecuted after he did not reply to the police letter The Three Lions star was convicted in the Single Justice Procedure, with a magistrate last week issuing him four penalty points and ordering him to pay a £666 fine, £120 in costs, and a £266 victim surcharge

title: Proposed Cheshire 60-hectare data centre sparks concerns

evidence_packet.title: Proposed Cheshire 60-hectare data centre sparks concerns
evidence_packet.lead: Residents say they are worried about issues including flooding, lighting and noise pollution
evidence_packet.summary: Residents say they are worried about issues including flooding, lighting and noise pollution
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A plan for a "massive" data centre close to a small village could claim a large area of land on the edge of the Cheshire countryside The scheme, which is earmarked for a space close to Little Bollington near Lymm has been put forward by a company called Innova Residents have been receiving leaflets about the bid in recent weeks, and some have told the BBC they are "extremely worried" about the potential impact on their homes, businesses and wildlife Data centres are typically large warehouses that store servers that process and distribute information online and the artificial intelligence boom has coincided with a significant increase in the number of proposals to build them But the Little Bollington plans – which have not been submitted for planning permission yet – are facing some opposition Janice Taylor, who runs Ash Farm bed and breakfast, said: "It's massive. evidence_packet.summary: Trespassers on the railway in the North West cost the taxpayer nearly £6m, Network Rail says

title: Salford Royal surgery unit fails to improve rating

evidence_packet.title: Salford Royal surgery unit fails to improve rating
evidence_packet.lead: Inspectors said patients were treated with kindness and compassion, but a range of concerns remained
evidence_packet.summary: Inspectors said patients were treated with kindness and compassion, but a range of concerns remained
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Surgery services at a Greater Manchester hospital have been rated as requiring improvement after an inspection found further work was needed to ensure patients received safe and timely care The Care Quality Commission (CQC) found Salford Royal Hospital had made enough progress to comply with a warning notice issued in October 2025 over staffing levels and risk management, but identified 12 breaches of regulations relating to patient safety, governance and staffing The inspection was carried out in May following concerns about staffing, governance and safety processes in gynaecology, spinal surgery and neurosurgery Karen Coverley, deputy chief nursing officer, said the trust was pleased inspectors had recognised improvements Inspectors said some staff had not completed life-support training relevant to their roles, infection-control standards remained below trust targets and incidents were not always investigated in a timely manner The report also highlighted concerns over waiting times, discharge delays and patient readmission rates following surgery

evidence_packet.summary: Sir Stephen Watson says next year's summit will be a 'vast' operation for Greater Manchester Police
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester's chief constable said hosting the G20 summit in 2027 will be a "vast policing operation" that will put pressure on resources Speaking to BBC Radio Manchester's Hotseat programme , Sir Stephen Watson said the event would "bring pressures" and added: "If we're not careful, it could sadly bend us out of shape." He said the international gathering would provide an opportunity to showcase the city on the world stage, but require a significant commitment of officers and resources Despite the scale of the operation, Sir Stephen said he was confident Greater Manchester Police and forces from across the UK would be able to deliver a successful security operation The G20 summit, an annual gathering of the world's biggest economies, will take place on 27 and 28 November 2027 at the Manchester Central Convention Centre It will be the largest summit ever held in the city and is expected to bring world leaders and their delegations to Manchester, along with thousands of journalists, officials, campaigners and protesters

title: Gun violence falls as shootings down by 77% in Greater Manchester

evidence_packet.title: Gun violence falls as shootings down by 77% in Greater Manchester
evidence_packet.lead: There were 16 firearms discharges in the 12 months to April 2026, compared with 71 incidents in 2020-21
evidence_packet.summary: There were 16 firearms discharges in the 12 months to April 2026, compared with 71 incidents in 2020-21
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Gun violence falls as shootings down by 77% in Greater Manchester - BBC News Image source, Greater Manchester Police Image caption, Many of the firearms recovered by Greater Manchester Police were converted from blank-firing weapons. By Richard Stead North West Published 29 September 2026 Shootings in Greater Manchester have fallen by more than three-quarters in the past five years, police figures show. According to Greater Manchester Police (GMP) figures, there were 16 firearms discharges in the 12 months to April 2026, down from 71 in 2020-21, a fall of 77.5% over five years. The force has also recovered more than 420 viable weapons since April 2021. It comes as Greater Manchester marks three-and-a-half years without a fatal shooting in the region. Det Supt Joe Harrop, head of serious and organised crime at GMP, said retaliatory shootings between rival groups had become less common because of the force's "robust police response". Firearms discharges fall In 2008, there were 146 shootings in Greater Manchester. This number had more than halved by 2020. Since then, firearms discharges across the region have continued to fall - albeit not consistently - and GMP data shows there has been a significant drop-off in gun violence rates betweens 2020 and 2026. Number of firearms discharges: 2020 to 2021 : 71 2021 to 2022 : 46 2022 to 2023 : 26 2023 to 2024 : 28 2024 to 2025 : 29 2025 to 2026 : 16 Since 1 April 2026 : 3 Image caption, Police say significant sentences for those convicted of gun crime has helped lower rates of offending Harrop said a crackdown on converted blank-firing weapons, alongside significant sentences for those convicted of gun crime, has also helped bring down rates of offending. title: Body building products seized in raids in Rochdale and Manchester

evidence_packet.title: Body building products seized in raids in Rochdale and Manchester
evidence_packet.lead: Up to a million tablets were confiscated during the raids on a suspects organised crime group
evidence_packet.summary: Up to a million tablets were confiscated during the raids on a suspects organised crime group
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Four people have been arrested after police seized what they believe could be up to one million illicit pharmaceutical drugs during raids linked to an organised crime group Three arrests were made at four addresses in Rochdale following a six-month investigation. A fourth person was arrested in Manchester Officers suspect the group was distributing drugs including diazepam, bodybuilding products and weight-loss medications across the UK Det Insp Rich McCorry said there were "serious dangers" associated with unlicensed drugs being sold to the public Two men aged 23 and 52 were arrested at an address on Twingate in Rochdale. A 51-year-old man was arrested on Whittaker Lane in the town, while a 44-year-old man was arrested on Kingsway in Manchester All four were arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to supply Class A, B and C drugs and remain in custody

evidence_packet.summary: Shootings in Greater Manchester have fallen by more than three-quarters in the past five years, police figures show According to Greater Manchester Police (GMP) figures, there were 16 firearms discharges in the 12 months to April 2026, down from 71 in 2020-21, a fall of 77.5% ove
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Shootings in Greater Manchester have fallen by more than three-quarters in the past five years, police figures show According to Greater Manchester Police (GMP) figures, there were 16 firearms discharges in the 12 months to April 2026, down from 71 in 2020-21, a fall of 77.5% over five years The force has also recovered more than 420 viable weapons since April 2021. It comes as Greater Manchester marks three-and-a-half years without a fatal shooting in the region Det Supt Joe Harrop, head of serious and organised crime at GMP, said retaliatory shootings between rival groups had become less common because of the force's "robust police response" In 2008, there were 146 shootings in Greater Manchester. This number had more than halved by 2020 Since then, firearms discharges across the region have continued to fall - albeit not consistently - and GMP data shows there has been a significant drop-off in gun violence rates betweens 2020 and 2026

The England defender had been caught speeding in his £150,000 Range Rover in May He was clocked driving at 43mph along a 30mph stretch of country lane near his Cheshire home. Stones, who left City for Inter Milan this summer, admitted being the driver when he was first contacted by Cheshire Police But the 32-year-old did not respond to a second letter from police, which offered him the chance to pay a fixed penalty to keep the speeding offence out of court . Stones told Warrington Magistrates Court the letter was 'found by chance' after his home was vacant for 'almost four In a written statement, Stones said he had 'nothing to say about the speeding' but added: "The reason I am only responding to the offence now is because I represent our country for football and so I have not been home and seen any post. I sent off my letter on the 28th May to giv “I went on holiday and then moved to Milan, so this has been found by chance, as no one has been home for almost four months. "I had to set up a direct debit for £35 a month," he said

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts John Stones taken to court after he's caught in £150,000 Range Rover near Cheshire home The former Man City footballer said no one had been at his home for 'almost four months' while he was at the World Cup Comments News Tristan Kirk, PA and St Former Manchester City star John Stones has been convicted of speeding after missing a police letter while at the World Cup . Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 18:39, 29 Sep 2026 As a Manchester City starlet, Courtney Meppen-Walter appeared to have the footballing world at his feet. The Bury-born defender and midfielder was attracting rave reviews turning out for the Blue's academy and Under-21 sides Snapped up by The Citizens at the age of just nine, his performances went on to earn him international call-ups. He represented England at Under-17 and Under-18 level, where he captained the side But tragedy struck in September, 2012, the fall-out from which went on to shape and taint his future career Meppen-Walter - who has died suddenly at the age of 32 - admitted causing the deaths of two people, a sister and brother while at the wheel of his grandad's Mercedes A court heard he was speeding at around 56mph in a 30mph zone when he ploughed into a Nissan Micra emerging from a side street at the junction of Great Ducie Street and Sherborne Street in Manchester city centre

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Health 'My sister saved my life, and we never even talked about it' "It is weird to think he has a piece of me in him, but I look at my scar and it's also like I have a piece of Harry with me forever" Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovati A Stockport woman has saved her brother's life after deciding to donate her kidney - without him ever asking For Rachel Ware, there was never any doubt that she would step in to save her brother Harry. The 24-year-old simply texted him the life-changing news "I guess some people might find it odd, but Rachel and I never had that conversation," said Harry, 22. "She never asked if I wanted her kidney and I never asked to have it. She spoke to my mum about it and just texted me saying she wanted to do it." The siblings say they have always been close, but when Harry became seriously ill while studying at university in London, that "special bond" took on a new significance. While at uni, Harry began to feel "weird". He suffered from bad cramps and needed the toilet more than usual View 5 Images Rachel and Harry Ware before Harry’s illness (Image: Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust)

evidence_packet.lead: A massive archive of work and personal items belonging to one of the greatest composers in British history has found a home in Manchester.
evidence_packet.summary: A massive archive of work and personal items belonging to one of the greatest composers in British history has found a home in Manchester. The Hallé orchestra is the new proud custodian of Sir Edward Elgar's never before seen manuscripts, personal photos and household objects A c
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A massive archive of work and personal items belonging to one of the greatest composers in British history has found a home in Manchester. The Hallé orchestra is the new proud custodian of Sir Edward Elgar's never before seen manuscripts, personal photos and household objects A collection that took 60 years to build, the previous owner was Arthur Reynolds, an American businessman and Elgar enthusiast who spent a lifetime sourcing the musician’s possessions before donating them to the Hallé Reynolds, who is also the chairman of the North American branch of the Elgar Society, has generously gifted around 1,500 meticulously preserved items to the orchestra "My overriding emotion is relief that these objects will be displayed properly and cared for in perpetuity," Reynolds told the M.E.N during a unveiling of the collection to members of the press and dignitaries at the Bridgwater Hall on Tuesday (September 29) The collection made it to Britain thanks to a large-scale operation that saw The National Heritage Memorial Fund award the Hallé nearly £105,000 to support the legal aspect and transport to the UK View 6 Images Elgar taking a break on some steps after a new piece from The Kingdom has been performed for his friends, 1906

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Northern 'Unreliable' Northern trains could be a thing of the past if Greater Manchester gets its way If the UK Government hands out the cash needed, up to 450 new trains could be running on train tracks across the region. Comments News Edward Barnes Northern Rail’s ‘ageing’ and ‘unreliable’ trains could soon be a thing of the past if Manchester transport bosses get their way Northern is currently bidding for funding which would see the rail operator’s largest ever investment in its fleet. If the UK Government hands out the cash needed, up to 450 new trains could be running on train tracks across the region If approved, the new trains would be introduced on a phased basis, replacing the oldest units in the fleet, most of which have been in service since the 1980s and 90s. Approximately two thirds of the existing fleet is targeted to be replaced in the next ten years According to Northern’s website, they hope to award contracts in 2027 with the first trains delivered by 2030. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Politics Andy Burnham's head in a box, singer's arrest and a human fox: Inside the Labour party conference protests It's a sensory overload, according to some attendees View 7 Images Andy Burnham's head in a box at the protests outside the Labour Conf Comments News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 11:07, 29 Sep 2026 Updated 11:25, 29 Sep 2026 A crude replica of Andy Burnham’s head lies in a shopping bag on the Liverpool Docks. In a nearby car park, a woman is getting dressed in a full-body fox get-up out of the back of These are just some of the sights that greeted attendees of the Labour Party Conference on their way into the Liverpool Experience Campus yesterday. Just as prominent as the frenetic energy of the conference itself - with attendees racing between venues and elbowing into the back Some of these have already had high-profile news coverage. On Sunday, Merseyside police arrested 82 protestors holding ‘I oppose genocide. I support Palestine Action’ signs “on suspicion of wearing/carrying an article supporting a proscribed organisation” Detainees included 94-year-old human rights barrister Margaret Owen and Massive Attack’s singer Robert Del Naja. The arrests were criticised by Amnesty International as ‘a shameful attack on freedom of speech’ Monday saw a smaller but enduring showing of Palestine protestors at the tail end of the security queue. They did not appear to hold any signs related to Palestine Action

title: Stepping Hill Hospital car park bosses speak out as patients slapped with incorrect £70 fines in 'absolute joke'

evidence_packet.title: Stepping Hill Hospital car park bosses speak out as patients slapped with incorrect £70 fines in 'absolute joke'
evidence_packet.lead: Stockport Stepping Hill Hospital car park bosses speak out as patients slapped with incorrect £70 fines in 'absolute joke' Drivers using the car park to visit loved ones at Stepping Hill Hospital have hit out after receiving 'farcical' fines Comments Two family members of patient
evidence_packet.summary: Stockport Stepping Hill Hospital car park bosses speak out as patients slapped with incorrect £70 fines in 'absolute joke' Drivers using the car park to visit loved ones at Stepping Hill Hospital have hit out after receiving 'farcical' fines Comments Two family members of patient
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Stepping Hill Hospital car park bosses speak out as patients slapped with incorrect £70 fines in 'absolute joke' Drivers using the car park to visit loved ones at Stepping Hill Hospital have hit out after receiving 'farcical' fines Comments Two family members of patients at Stepping Hill Hospital have hit out after being wrongly issued parking fines Terry Wansell and Emily Heward say they both received tickets in the post after paying to park at the hospital in Stockport this summer and had to endure an arduous process to have them overturned Terry, 59, from Great Moor, was fined twice, the first time as he took his son to A&E with a serious hand injury in March this year. Terry, who works in the care sector, said he paid for a ticket, but didn't keep hold of it, before a letter regarding a parking charge notice (PCN) He claims he never received an initial letter about the fine, that the first letter he received stated he had lost his right of appeal, and that, as a result, the amount he owed increased, leading him to pay a total of £160 Terry said he was unsure whether he was within the time he paid for, or a couple of minutes over but that without his ticket and with no right of appeal, he felt unable to fight it. "I had to set up a direct debit for £35 a month," he said

evidence_packet.lead: Courts John Stones taken to court after he's caught in £150,000 Range Rover near Cheshire home The former Man City footballer said no one had been at his home for 'almost four months' while he was at the World Cup Comments News Tristan Kirk, PA and St Former Manchester City star
evidence_packet.summary: Courts John Stones taken to court after he's caught in £150,000 Range Rover near Cheshire home The former Man City footballer said no one had been at his home for 'almost four months' while he was at the World Cup Comments News Tristan Kirk, PA and St Former Manchester City star
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts John Stones taken to court after he's caught in £150,000 Range Rover near Cheshire home The former Man City footballer said no one had been at his home for 'almost four months' while he was at the World Cup Comments News Tristan Kirk, PA and St Former Manchester City star John Stones has been convicted of speeding after missing a police letter while at the World Cup . The England defender had been caught speeding in his £150,000 Range Rover in May He was clocked driving at 43mph along a 30mph stretch of country lane near his Cheshire home. Stones, who left City for Inter Milan this summer, admitted being the driver when he was first contacted by Cheshire Police But the 32-year-old did not respond to a second letter from police, which offered him the chance to pay a fixed penalty to keep the speeding offence out of court . Stones told Warrington Magistrates Court the letter was 'found by chance' after his home was vacant for 'almost four In a written statement, Stones said he had 'nothing to say about the speeding' but added: "The reason I am only responding to the offence now is because I represent our country for football and so I have not been home and seen any post. I sent off my letter on the 28th May to giv “I went on holiday and then moved to Milan, so this has been found by chance, as no one has been home for almost four months. This is the reason I also would not be able to be present as I no longer am residing in the country.”

None have been detailed The charity, which monitors antisemitism in Britain, noted that the latest figures are lower than the 'unprecedented' 272 incidents reported during the academic year of 2023/24. Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 18:39, 29 Sep 2026 As a Manchester City starlet, Courtney Meppen-Walter appeared to have the footballing world at his feet. The Bury-born defender and midfielder was attracting rave reviews turning out for the Blue's academy and Under-21 sides Snapped up by The Citizens at the age of just nine, his performances went on to earn him international call-ups. He represented England at Under-17 and Under-18 level, where he captained the side But tragedy struck in September, 2012, the fall-out from which went on to shape and taint his future career Meppen-Walter - who has died suddenly at the age of 32 - admitted causing the deaths of two people, a sister and brother while at the wheel of his grandad's Mercedes A court heard he was speeding at around 56mph in a 30mph zone when he ploughed into a Nissan Micra emerging from a side street at the junction of Great Ducie Street and Sherborne Street in Manchester city centre

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Health 'My sister saved my life, and we never even talked about it' "It is weird to think he has a piece of me in him, but I look at my scar and it's also like I have a piece of Harry with me forever" Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovati A Stockport woman has saved her brother's life after deciding to donate her kidney - without him ever asking For Rachel Ware, there was never any doubt that she would step in to save her brother Harry. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A massive archive of work and personal items belonging to one of the greatest composers in British history has found a home in Manchester. The Hallé orchestra is the new proud custodian of Sir Edward Elgar's never before seen manuscripts, personal photos and household objects A collection that took 60 years to build, the previous owner was Arthur Reynolds, an American businessman and Elgar enthusiast who spent a lifetime sourcing the musician’s possessions before donating them to the Hallé Reynolds, who is also the chairman of the North American branch of the Elgar Society, has generously gifted around 1,500 meticulously preserved items to the orchestra "My overriding emotion is relief that these objects will be displayed properly and cared for in perpetuity," Reynolds told the M.E.N during a unveiling of the collection to members of the press and dignitaries at the Bridgwater Hall on Tuesday (September 29) The collection made it to Britain thanks to a large-scale operation that saw The National Heritage Memorial Fund award the Hallé nearly £105,000 to support the legal aspect and transport to the UK View 6 Images Elgar taking a break on some steps after a new piece from The Kingdom has been performed for his friends, 1906

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Northern 'Unreliable' Northern trains could be a thing of the past if Greater Manchester gets its way If the UK Government hands out the cash needed, up to 450 new trains could be running on train tracks across the region. Comments News Edward Barnes Northern Rail’s ‘ageing’ and ‘unreliable’ trains could soon be a thing of the past if Manchester transport bosses get their way Northern is currently bidding for funding which would see the rail operator’s largest ever investment in its fleet. If the UK Government hands out the cash needed, up to 450 new trains could be running on train tracks across the region If approved, the new trains would be introduced on a phased basis, replacing the oldest units in the fleet, most of which have been in service since the 1980s and 90s. Approximately two thirds of the existing fleet is targeted to be replaced in the next ten years According to Northern’s website, they hope to award contracts in 2027 with the first trains delivered by 2030. A total of 130 new trains would be delivered as part of phase one over three years replacing trains at or near ‘the end of their life’ An update was given on the major investment plan at a recent Bee Network committee meeting following questions on transport issues across Greater Manchester

title: Motion tabled to celebrate centenary of women's voting equality

evidence_packet.title: Motion tabled to celebrate centenary of women's voting equality
evidence_packet.lead: In 2028 it will be 100 years since women were granted the right to vote on equal terms with men
evidence_packet.summary: In 2028 it will be 100 years since women were granted the right to vote on equal terms with men
evidence_packet.evidence_text: In 2028 it will be 100 years since women were granted the right to vote on equal terms with men Although some women were granted the right to vote in 1918, it was not until 1928 that all women over the age of 21 were granted the vote regardless of their occupation, wealth or ownership of property To mark this hugely significant milestone a Council motion has been set out to recognise and celebrate this moment in history It is no secret that Manchester played a huge part in the Women’s Suffrage movement. The Pankhurst name is known across the globe and is a byword for resilience and a refusal to give in to apparent insurmountable odds In 2018 a statue of Emmeline Pankhurst was proudly installed in St Peter’s Square and has since become a rallying point for people across the city to have their voices heard, and acts as a powerful reminder that history was made by women who refused to give up But the Pankhursts were also joined by thousands of ordinary Mancunian women whose names have been lost to history, but whose legacy still lives on a century later

title: New Deputy Leader appointed at Manchester City Council

evidence_packet.summary: Cllr Thomas Robinson has been chosen as the new Deputy Leader of Manchester City Council
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cllr Thomas Robinson has been chosen as the new Deputy Leader of Manchester City Council He fills the role vacated by Cllr Garry Bridges when he was elected Leader earlier this month and will serve alongside the other Deputy Leader, Cllr Tracey Rawlins His portfolio responsibilities will include work and skills, crime and safety and emergency planning Cllr Robinson has served as Executive Member for Health and Social Care since 2022 overseeing the adult social care service which was recently rated ‘Good’ by the Care Quality Commission, and has represented Clayton and Openshaw as a councillor since 2021 Raised in Ardwick, he has deep roots in Manchester and his experience growing up in a council flat amid a supportive community has shaped his commitment to public service and building a city where everyone can thrive regardless of background “As a born and bred Mancunian, to become the Deputy Leader of our city is truly humbling. In supporting Councillor Bridges as Leader, I promise to continue to put the voices of our communities as the heart of every decision we take in their service.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The skies over Manchester will light up once again as firework night celebrations are set to return with displays in Manchester parks this year bringing the city’s communities together On Saturday 7 November, free family-friendly fireworks events at Wythenshawe Park, Heaton Park and Platt Fields Park will feature both a reduced-noise, low-impact display at 5pm for families and SEND audiences and a main fireworks display at 8pm, with accessibility and inclusivit Each of the three parks will host lantern making workshops in the weeks leading up to the events, with family-friendly lantern parades taking place ahead of the 8pm firework shows. Additional entertainment will be announced for each park in the coming weeks Major fireworks events had been paused in 2019 following the Covid-19 pandemic when funding challenges spurred a change of direction with the Council choosing to invest in a range of community focused events across the city’s parks through the autumn season – rather than the majo The good news is that these community focused events will still take place and are set to expand further in local parks this year, particularly in the run up to and during the October half term school holiday, with a mix of themed activities. Further details will be announced in With additional Council investment, the fireworks events on November 7 will be a grand finale to the community activities happening across the city

Officers spoke to those at the encampment, who said they intended to leave by Saturday 8th August As the site had not been vacated, the Council returned with support from Greater Manchester Police on Tuesday 11th August. A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Council has announced that it intends to appoint Acumen Waste Services Limited to clear the illegal waste site at Bolton House Road in Bickershaw, subject to contract Over the past few weeks, the council has been leading the procurement process to find the most suitable contractor to clear the entire site, with applicants asked to explain how they will safely remove the waste and manage associated risks Following the robust tender process, Acumen Waste Services Limited has been chosen as the preferred contractor. There will now be a compulsory standstill period and the contract is expected to be signed in early October, with mobilisation to remove the waste planned to start in l Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental services, and transport, said: “The scale of the illegal waste site at Bolton House Road has had a devastating impact on the local community, so I am delighted that we are now in a position to appoint a contracto “The appointment is a significant milestone, but residents should have never been put into this position, and we will continue to support the Environment Agency’s criminal investigation to punish those responsible for this environmental destruction.” Following an emergency response to a fire that broke out and lasted for several days in July 2025, a multi-agency partnership group was set up to manage the illegal waste site, prevent further waste deposits, and minimise the impact on the public and the environment

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.summary: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live […] The post Beat the Jams Autumn season announced appeared first on Band on the Wall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

Both have official sh Built in 2000 at the booming Salford Quays, this astonishing building is a shrine to all things art, with galleries, theatres, workshops, cafes and shops. It's worth a visit just to sit outside and admire the vision in metal and glass. But you'd be missing out on a whole world of Watersports The Salford Watersports Centre at The Quays is a unique sporting venue which is well placed and perfect for taking to the water. title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital

evidence_packet.title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital
evidence_packet.lead: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing.
evidence_packet.summary: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Digital’s MD Future 26 conference brought together industry leaders, academia, founders, investors and policymakers, to look at the businesses and technologies shaping the next phase of the region’s tech economy Held at Campfield Studios, the newly restored former Victorian produce and exhibition hall, which was completed at the end of the city’s Industrial Revolution, the venue offered a striking backdrop for discussions about Manchester’s role in today’s AI and digital transformation Across a day covering physical AI, infrastructure, cyber security, health, space and quantum, some clear themes came through. The next phase of AI is likely to be much less about what a model can demonstrate on a screen and much more about whether businesses can deploy it securel There is also an opportunity for Manchester and the wider North that goes beyond simply increasing AI adoption. The region already has strengths across advanced materials, computing infrastructure, cyber security, health innovation and emerging technologies such as quantum. The c The previous day also saw an Innovation Day, where 20 of the region’s most innovative startups pitched to the biggest organisations working across defence, national security and technology, then took part in a number of Round Table discussions Here’s our write up of the full day’s conference

evidence_packet.summary: This September, MD Future 26 brings together leaders, innovators and experts from across the technology ecosystem to explore the emerging technologies and ideas set to shape our economy and society in the years ahead From AI and digital infrastructure to deep tech, cyber security
evidence_packet.evidence_text: This September, MD Future 26 brings together leaders, innovators and experts from across the technology ecosystem to explore the emerging technologies and ideas set to shape our economy and society in the years ahead From AI and digital infrastructure to deep tech, cyber security, talent and innovation, the pace of change presents huge opportunities for organisations - but also raises important questions about where to invest, what to prioritise and how to prepare for what comes next Ahead of the conference, we asked contributors from across our membership to answer one question: What’s the next big shift in technology — and how should businesses prepare? Here, they share their perspectives on the trends they believe will have the greatest impact, the opportunities and challenges ahead, and what organisations should be thinking about now to stay ready for the future Part Two , featuring more perspectives from across the ecosystem, can be read here MD Future 26 is sponsored by Pulsant , Novacoast with Platform Markets Group and CTI Digital , with support from Department and UK Tech Cluster Group

evidence_packet.summary: For almost a year, T Connect students have been joining us in the Manchester Digital office and getting a taste of what it really means to build a career in tech. It’s been a pleasure to have them with us
evidence_packet.evidence_text: For almost a year, T Connect students have been joining us in the Manchester Digital office and getting a taste of what it really means to build a career in tech. It’s been a pleasure to have them with us. We’ve seen their curiosity, eagerness and passion for technology, as well But the success of T Connect has never been something Manchester Digital could deliver alone At its heart, T Connect is about building meaningful connections between technical education and the technology sector. That means giving students opportunities to meet people working in the industry, understand the different careers available to them and, crucially, put their sk Over the past year, businesses and individuals from across our community have helped make that possible in a huge variety of ways - from industry insight sessions and technical masterclasses to mentoring, work experience, office visits and live business projects Our students had the opportunity to learn directly from industry professionals, developing their technical knowledge and getting insight into the tools and approaches used in the workplace Hyperact - Jacob Clark, Director of Engineering, delivered a JavaScript masterclass, helping students strengthen their practical technical knowledge

The concert will feature Beethoven’s Symphony No. 6, the Pastoral Symphony The Cadenza project, led by the University of Salford, is researching how to improve music for people with hearing loss. The free concert is a unique opportunity to shape future research on hearing aids while enjoying live music Trevor Cox, Professor of acoustic engineering at the University of Salford, explains: “We don’t think anything like this has been attempted before. When people suffer hearing loss, the main treatment is a hearing aid. But the devices are designed for speech. Music is an afterthou “But music is such an important part of our lives, it brings us together for shared experiences that people with hearing issues can feel locked out of. Live classical music is particularly hard for hearing aids to deal with, as it ranges from extremely quiet to very louder, over “This is a unique opportunity for people, both with hearing problems and those who hear normally, to help shape future research on hearing aids while enjoying the fabulous Camerata.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. title: Courtney Meppen-Walter: From future Man City star to tragedy

evidence_packet.title: Courtney Meppen-Walter: From future Man City star to tragedy
evidence_packet.lead: Football clubs have issued statements after his sudden death aged 32
evidence_packet.summary: Football clubs have issued statements after his sudden death aged 32
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City FC Courtney Meppen-Walter: From future Man City star to tragedy Football clubs have issued statements after his sudden death aged 32 View 7 Images Courtney Meppen-Walter (Image: GMP/M.E.N.) Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 18:39, 29 Sep 2026 As a Manchester City starlet, Courtney Meppen-Walter appeared to have the footballing world at his feet. The Bury-born defender and midfielder was attracting rave reviews turning out for the Blue's academy and Under-21 sides Snapped up by The Citizens at the age of just nine, his performances went on to earn him international call-ups. He represented England at Under-17 and Under-18 level, where he captained the side But tragedy struck in September, 2012, the fall-out from which went on to shape and taint his future career Meppen-Walter - who has died suddenly at the age of 32 - admitted causing the deaths of two people, a sister and brother while at the wheel of his grandad's Mercedes A court heard he was speeding at around 56mph in a 30mph zone when he ploughed into a Nissan Micra emerging from a side street at the junction of Great Ducie Street and Sherborne Street in Manchester city centre
